title: Money & Financial Mathematics
description: Calculating with money, profit and loss, simple interest, budgets, best buys and value for money.

notes.heading: Money and Decimal Calculations
notes.body:
📌 Definition
Money amounts are written using decimals. The digits before the decimal point represent whole dollars (or other currency units) and the digits after represent cents. For example, $\$12.45$ means $12$ dollars and $45$ cents.

🔑 Key Concept
When adding or subtracting money, line up the decimal points. When multiplying, count the total number of decimal places in the factors to place the decimal point in the answer.

💡 Worked Example
Calculate the total cost of three items priced $\$4.25$, $\$7.80$ and $\$3.99$.

Step 1: Add the amounts
$$4.25 + 7.80 + 3.99 = 16.04$$
The total cost is $\$16.04$.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Always use two decimal places for cents, even when the second digit is zero (e.g. $\$5.20$).
• Rounding money to the nearest cent means rounding to two decimal places.
• Use estimation first to check your answer is reasonable.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Misplacing the decimal point when multiplying. For example, $\$2.50 \times 3$ should be $\$7.50$, not $\$75.00$.

notes.heading: Profit and Loss
notes.body:
📌 Definition
Profit is the amount of money made when an item is sold for more than it cost. Loss is the amount of money lost when an item is sold for less than it cost.

🔑 Key Concept
$$\text{Profit} = \text{Selling Price} - \text{Cost Price}$$
$$\text{Loss} = \text{Cost Price} - \text{Selling Price}$$
If the selling price is higher than the cost price, you make a profit. If it is lower, you make a loss.

💡 Worked Example
A shop buys a book for $\$15$ and sells it for $\$22$. Find the profit.

Step 1: Identify the cost price and selling price
Cost price $= \$15$, Selling price $= \$22$

Step 2: Subtract
$$\text{Profit} = 22 - 15 = 7$$
The profit is $\$7$.

✅ Check
Since the selling price is greater than the cost price, the answer should be positive and represent a profit.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Forgetting to state whether the final amount is a profit or a loss. Always include the correct word or sign with your answer.

notes.heading: Percentage Profit and Loss
notes.body:
📌 Definition
Percentage profit or loss compares the amount of profit or loss to the original cost price, written as a percentage.

🔑 Key Concept
$$\text{Percentage Profit} = \dfrac{\text{Profit}}{\text{Cost Price}} \times 100\%$$
$$\text{Percentage Loss} = \dfrac{\text{Loss}}{\text{Cost Price}} \times 100\%$$
The cost price is always used as the denominator because it is the original amount invested.

💡 Worked Example
A bicycle is bought for $\$200$ and sold for $\$250$. Calculate the percentage profit.

Step 1: Find the profit
$$\text{Profit} = 250 - 200 = 50$$

Step 2: Divide by the cost price and multiply by $100\%$
$$\text{Percentage Profit} = \dfrac{50}{200} \times 100\% = 25\%$$

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Percentage profit and loss are always calculated on the cost price, not the selling price.
• A percentage greater than $100\%$ means the profit is larger than the original cost.
• Convert fractions to decimals before multiplying by $100\%$ if needed.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Using the selling price as the denominator instead of the cost price. This gives a different and incorrect percentage.

notes.heading: Simple Interest
notes.body:
📌 Definition
Simple interest is money paid for borrowing or earned from saving, calculated as a fixed percentage of the principal amount each year.

🔑 How it works
The formula for simple interest is:
$$I = P \times R \times T$$
where:
• $I$ = interest
• $P$ = principal (the initial amount of money)
• $R$ = annual interest rate as a decimal
• $T$ = time in years

The total amount after interest is:
$$A = P + I$$

💡 Worked Example
Sofia invests $\$500$ at $4\%$ per annum simple interest for $3$ years. How much interest does she earn?

Step 1: Convert the rate to a decimal
$$R = 4\% = 0.04$$

Step 2: Substitute into the formula
$$I = 500 \times 0.04 \times 3 = 60$$
Sofia earns $\$60$ in interest.

✅ Check
Each year she earns $500 \times 0.04 = \$20$. Over $3$ years this is $3 \times 20 = \$60$, which matches the formula.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Forgetting to convert the percentage rate to a decimal before substituting. $4\%$ becomes $0.04$, not $4$.

notes.heading: Discounts and Sale Prices
notes.body:
📌 Definition
A discount is a reduction in the original price of an item. The sale price is the price after the discount has been taken off.

🔑 Key Concept
$$\text{Discount Amount} = \text{Original Price} \times \dfrac{\text{Discount \%}}{100}$$
$$\text{Sale Price} = \text{Original Price} - \text{Discount Amount}$$
Alternatively, you can find what percentage of the price you will actually pay and multiply by the original price.

💡 Worked Example
A jacket originally costs $\$80$ and is reduced by $25\%$. Find the sale price.

Step 1: Find the discount amount
$$80 \times 0.25 = 20$$
The discount is $\$20$.

Step 2: Subtract from the original price
$$80 - 20 = 60$$
The sale price is $\$60$.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• $25\%$ off means you pay $75\%$ of the original price.
• A second discount is usually calculated on the already-reduced price, not the original price.
• Always check whether the question asks for the discount amount or the final sale price.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Finding the discount but then forgetting to subtract it from the original price, or subtracting the percentage directly instead of the dollar amount.

notes.heading: Best Buys and Unit Price
notes.body:
📌 Definition
A best buy is the purchase option that gives the most product for the least money. The unit price is the cost of one unit of an item, such as one gram or one millilitre.

🔑 How it works
To compare different sized packages, calculate the unit price for each:
$$\text{Unit Price} = \dfrac{\text{Total Price}}{\text{Number of Units}}$$
The option with the lowest unit price is usually the best value, provided you can use all of the product.

💡 Worked Example
A $500$ gram pack of cereal costs $\$4.50$, while a $750$ gram pack costs $\$6.30$. Which is the better buy?

Step 1: Find the unit price per gram for each pack
Small pack: $\dfrac{4.50}{500} = 0.009$ dollars per gram
Large pack: $\dfrac{6.30}{750} = 0.0084$ dollars per gram

Step 2: Compare
$0.0084 < 0.009$, so the $750$ gram pack is the better buy.

✅ Check
The larger pack costs $1.5$ times as much but contains $1.5$ times as much cereal, yet the total price is less than $1.5 \times 4.50 = \$6.75$, confirming it is better value.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Assuming the larger pack is always better value. Always calculate the unit price before deciding.

notes.heading: Budgets
notes.body:
📌 Definition
A budget is a plan that shows expected income and expenses over a period of time. It helps people manage money and avoid spending more than they earn.

🔑 Key Concept
$$\text{Total Income} - \text{Total Expenses} = \text{Surplus or Deficit}$$
If income is greater than expenses, there is a surplus. If expenses are greater than income, there is a deficit.

💡 Worked Example
Alex earns $\$120$ per week from a part-time job. His weekly expenses are $\$45$ for transport, $\$30$ for food and $\$20$ for entertainment. Does he have a surplus or deficit?

Step 1: Find total expenses
$$45 + 30 + 20 = 95$$
Total expenses are $\$95$.

Step 2: Compare with income
$$120 - 95 = 25$$
Alex has a surplus of $\$25$ per week.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• List every source of income and every expense, even small ones.
• Fixed expenses stay the same each period, while variable expenses can change.
• A surplus can be saved; a deficit means spending must be reduced.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Forgetting to include occasional expenses, such as a monthly phone bill, when making a weekly budget. Convert all amounts to the same time period first.

flashcards.definition: The amount of money made when an item is sold for more than it cost.
flashcards.example: Buying a book for $\$15$ and selling it for $\$22$ gives a profit of $\$7$.

flashcards.definition: The amount of money lost when an item is sold for less than it cost.
flashcards.example: Buying a toy for $\$30$ and selling it for $\$18$ gives a loss of $\$12$.

flashcards.definition: The original price paid to buy or produce an item.
flashcards.example: A shop pays $\$50$ for a shirt; $\$50$ is the cost price.

flashcards.definition: The price at which an item is sold to a customer.
flashcards.example: The shirt is sold to a customer for $\$75$; $\$75$ is the selling price.

flashcards.definition: Profit expressed as a percentage of the cost price.
flashcards.example: Profit of $\$50$ on a cost price of $\$200$ is $\dfrac{50}{200} \times 100\% = 25\%$.

flashcards.definition: Interest calculated as a fixed percentage of the principal each year.
The initial amount of money invested or borrowed.
flashcards.example: In a savings account, the $\$500$ deposit is the principal.

flashcards.definition: A reduction from the original price of an item.
flashcards.example: $25\%$ off a $\$80$ jacket is a $\$20$ discount.

flashcards.definition: The price paid after a discount is applied.
flashcards.example: A $\$80$ jacket with a $\$20$ discount has a sale price of $\$60$.

flashcards.definition: The cost of one unit of a product, such as one gram or one litre.
flashcards.example: A $\$6$ bottle containing $2$ litres has a unit price of $\$3$ per litre.

flashcards.definition: The purchase option that gives the lowest unit price and therefore the best value.
flashcards.example: A larger box with a lower cost per gram is the best buy.

flashcards.definition: The amount left over when total income is greater than total expenses.
flashcards.example: Earning $\$120$ and spending $\$95$ gives a surplus of $\$25$.

questions.stem: A pen costs $\$2.45$ and a notebook costs $\$3.85$. What is the total cost?
A shop buys a watch for $\$40$ and sells it for $\$65$. What is the profit?
questions.explanation: Profit equals selling price minus cost price: $\$65 - \$40 = \$25$.

questions.stem: A phone case costs $\$20$ to make and sells for $\$14$. What is the loss?
questions.explanation: Loss equals cost price minus selling price: $\$20 - \$14 = \$6$.

questions.stem: An item is bought for $\$80$ and sold for $\$100$. What is the percentage profit?
questions.explanation: The profit is $\$20$. Percentage profit is $\dfrac{20}{80} \times 100\% = 25\%$.

questions.stem: A bicycle bought for $\$250$ is sold for $\$200$. What is the percentage loss?
questions.explanation: The loss is $\$50$. Percentage loss is $\dfrac{50}{250} \times 100\% = 20\%$.

questions.stem: Calculate the simple interest on $\$600$ invested at $5\%$ per year for $4$ years.
A loan of $\$1000$ attracts $6\%$ simple interest per year. How much interest is owed after $2$ years?
A pair of shoes priced $\$90$ is discounted by $20\%$. What is the sale price?
A book is reduced from $\$30$ to $\$24$. What is the percentage discount?
questions.explanation: The discount amount is $\$6$. Percentage discount is $\dfrac{6}{30} \times 100\% = 20\%$.

questions.stem: Which is the better buy: $400$ grams for $\$5.60$ or $500$ grams for $\$7.00$?
questions.explanation: $400$ grams costs $5.60 \div 400 = \$0.014$ per gram; $500$ grams costs $7.00 \div 500 = \$0.014$ per gram. They have the same unit price, so they are equal value.

questions.stem: A $2$ litre bottle of juice costs $\$5.40$ and a $1.5$ litre bottle costs $\$3.90$. Which has the lower unit price?
questions.explanation: The $2$ litre unit price is $5.40 \div 2 = \$2.70$ per litre. The $1.5$ litre unit price is $3.90 \div 1.5 = \$2.60$ per litre, so the $1.5$ litre bottle has the lower unit price.

questions.stem: Mia earns $\$150$ per week and spends $\$35$ on food, $\$40$ on transport and $\$50$ on other expenses. What is her weekly surplus?
questions.explanation: Total expenses are $35 + 40 + 50 = \$125$. The surplus is $150 - 125 = \$25$.

questions.stem: An item costing $\$120$ is sold at a loss of $10\%$. What is the selling price?
How much money must be invested at $8\%$ simple interest for $3$ years to earn $\$72$ in interest?
A $\$50$ item has $10\%$ off, followed by another $10\%$ off the reduced price. What is the final price?
questions.explanation: After the first discount the price is $\$45$. The second discount is $10\%$ of $\$45$, which is $\$4.50$. The final price is $\$45 - \$4.50 = \$40.50$.
